outcome: N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels
cohort: The study included 320 antenatal women beyond 20 weeks of pregnancy, with 160 women diagnosed with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) as cases and 160 normotensive women as controls.
finding: Women with HDP showed significant differences in left ventricular structure and function, with lower ejection fraction and higher NT-proBNP levels correlating with maternal complications and adverse neonatal outcomes, highlighting the utility of these assessments in detecting early cardiac dysfunction in severe HDP.
gest_age: Beyond 20 weeks of pregnancy (for mothers at enrollment)
